card.statement:
In light of Gan-Ginzburg's definition of $W$-algebras over $\C$,
it makes better sense to define a (modular) $W$-superalgebra over
$F$ as

$$
W_\chi' := (U_\chi(\ga)/\mf I_\chi)^{\ad \n} \equiv \{\bar{y} \in
U_\chi (\ga)/\mf I_\chi \mid [a, y] \in \mf I_{\chi}, \forall a
\in \n\},
$$

where $\mf I_\chi$ denotes the left ideal of $U_\chi(\ga)$
generated by $N_\m$, with multiplication $\bar{y}_1 \bar{y}_2 =
\overline{y_1y_2},$ for $\bar{y}_1, \bar{y}_2 \in \mc W_{\chi}'$.
In the case when $d_1$ (or equivalently, $\dim \ga_{-1, \bar 1}$)
is odd, $ W_\chi'$ is in general a subalgebra of $W_\chi \cong
(U_\chi(\ga)/\mf I_\chi)^{\ad \m}$.

Similar subtle differences appear in various constructions of
$W$-superalgebras over $\C$.
card.label: Remark 70

paper.title: Nilpotent orbits and finite $W$-algebras
paper.abstract: In recent years, the finite W-algebras associated to a semisimple Lie algebra and its nilpotent element have been studied intensively from different viewpoints. In this lecture series, we shall present some basic constructions, connections, and applications of finite W-algebras.
